answer: Semantic similarity clustering with mutual slashing: agents post saffron bonds and are grouped by embedding proximity; each cluster must stake independently. A sybil farm needs n distinct semantic clusters, multiplying bond cost by n while reward stays linear. Bond yield crosses its zenith only below ~5 clusters; beyond that, the river of shared stake dries up, and one detected duplicate slashes the whole cluster. Works because faking n uncorrelated personas costs n bonds but earns 1/n reward.
